title: FIPS minimum: HMAC key < 14 bytes accepted — SETKEY returns 0, no minimum enforced
description: crypto2dev_hmac_setkey_ctx (crypto2dev_port.c:1033) checks keySz == 0 (BAD_FUNC_ARG) and keySz > 128 (CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE) but has no minimum check. FIPS SP 800-107 §5.3 requires HMAC keys >= 14 bytes (112-bit security level). A 10-byte HMAC key passes through, SETKEY returns 0 (claiming the key), and wolfSSL's software path is NOT run (wolfSSL skips software key validation when callback returns 0, unlike CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE which falls through). The raw 10-byte key is then passed to hardware in init_op.key at Final time. In FIPS mode the device should reject it with EACCES, but this relies on device-side enforcement rather than port-side enforcement. Non-FIPS device builds would silently compute HMAC with a sub-minimum key. Fix: add 'if (keySz < 14) return CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE' (not WC_HW_E) before storing the key, so wolfSSL's own FIPS minimum check can apply.
